# phron_storage_bucket (Resource)

An S3-compatible bucket in Phron Object Storage. The first bucket of a Workspace also creates its storage in the given Location (which needs a positive balance). Destroying the bucket needs it to be empty.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phron_storage_bucket" "logs" {
  name     = "logs"
  location = "fsn1" # an id from data.phron_storage_overview.this.locations

  object_lock                        = true
  object_lock_default_retention_days = 30
  limit_bytes                        = 1000000000000
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The bucket name. In a shared Cell this is only the part after the Cell's bucket name prefix (at most 52 characters); full_name carries the whole name.

### Optional

- `limit_bytes` (Number) Optional size limit in bytes, a spend guard. Do not combine with a phron_storage_bucket_limit resource for the same bucket.
- `location` (String) The Location id of the storage. Required when creating the Workspace's first storage while more than one Location is offered, and when the Workspace has storage in two Locations.
- `object_lock` (Boolean) Make the bucket Object Lock enabled (Governance mode). It can only be set when the bucket is created; changing it replaces the bucket.
- `object_lock_default_retention_days` (Number) Default retention in days for a lock-enabled bucket. Unset: none.
- `workspace_id` (String) The Workspace the bucket belongs to. Empty means the Organization's default Workspace.

### Read-Only

- `full_name` (String) The complete bucket name as S3 tools use it (the Cell's prefix plus name).
- `id` (String) The bucket's full name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import phron_storage_bucket.logs <full bucket name>
```
